phase: Prompt-only A solutions before authored keys/final HTML/prior findings
selection_rationale: All 31 guided/tricky A tasks selected because the new social/cultural, modality, text-type, paragraph and navigation families include interpretive or scope-boundary risk. All 10 A FAQs and activity/tier criteria also selected. Exact navigation execution and absent extra cards remain held.

solutions.AC9E3LA01-guided-1: Which tray did you mean? Do we put the blue label on before we fill the tray? Accept respectful clarification of the missed tray detail and a genuine order check.
solutions.AC9E3LA01-guided-2: Remember/write the question and wait for the invitation, or ask afterwards as offered. At an appropriate opportunity ask Could you tell me when/how we should ask questions? Respect this stated fictional arrangement rather than generalising it to every host/community.
solutions.AC9E3LA01-guided-3: Your idea keeps the labels together. Could we put each label beside its object so visitors can tell which name belongs to which model? Have we finished deciding the labels; could we choose the title next? Equivalent respectful reasoned suggestion plus negotiated transition acceptable.
solutions.AC9E3LA01-tricky-1: Yes. Attend to the contribution, explain a relevant reason and propose a workable alternative respectfully.
solutions.AC9E3LA01-tricky-2: Yes, depending on context and agreed conventions. Polite short words can suit both; turn-taking arrangements can differ.
solutions.AC9E3LA01-tricky-3: No. Check that host's/local community's arrangements for the actual occasion.
solutions.AC9E3LA02-guided-1: Could offers a possible choice; must would make a requirement in this context. Might presents possible arrival with uncertainty; will presents arrival as a more confident prediction, not proof that it will happen.
solutions.AC9E3LA02-guided-2: Told/ordered differ in force; calmly/angrily expressly change manner/attitude. A neutral version is The captain told the crew to wait. Do not preserve an asserted feeling while claiming neutrality.
solutions.AC9E3LA02-guided-3: Persistent fits continued effort and changing the base after failure. Rae felt delighted expresses stronger pleasure; terrified changes kind to fear and is not acceptable for that request.
solutions.AC9E3LA02-tricky-1: No in the ordinary rule context. Must not prohibits an action; do not have to removes the requirement but permits a choice. Context still matters for other uses of must.
solutions.AC9E3LA02-tricky-2: Yes. Different readers/narrators may evaluate an action differently; each explanation must be supported by the actual context and cannot contradict supplied facts.
solutions.AC9E3LA02-tricky-3: An emotion word by itself does not specify prediction certainty. Pleased/worried expresses feeling; might/will can express a prediction's degree of commitment in context.
solutions.AC9E3LA03-guided-1: Both organise experiences/events in time and use past events/time links. A is a reporter's recount of a particular team event with third-person they; B is an explicitly fictional model of a personal life account in I voice, selecting repeated personal learning and ending with current enjoyment. These choices suit event recording versus personal experience/reflection; I alone is insufficient proof of nonfiction autobiography.
solutions.AC9E3LA03-guided-2: Report: Materials heading groups the fact Both boxes are cardboard. Explanation: First and If the label says card... show the sorting sequence/condition; the final sentence explains keeping card together. A reader uses grouped facts for materials and process/condition links for how the prepared system works.
solutions.AC9E3LA03-guided-3: Little label uses verse lines and the imagined telling without a voice. Example personal response: I liked Bea helping Ari because she found the label under the cloth and they could label the boat before visitors came. Other supported reactions acceptable.
solutions.AC9E3LA03-guided-4: Introduction: We should put names on our model labels. Reason 1: visitors see who made each model. Reason 2: a visitor with a question can find its maker. Conclusion: Let's add our first names before the display opens. Rectangular merely describes shape and does not explain the value of names.
solutions.AC9E3LA03-tricky-1: No. Fictional first-person narrators use I; check author/account context and whose life is described.
solutions.AC9E3LA03-tricky-2: No. Recounts or instructions may be ordered too. An explanation shows how/why a process/result occurs through connected stages, not just first/next words.
solutions.AC9E3LA03-tricky-3: No. Offer your own reaction grounded in actual text events/details; a model demonstrates support rather than one compulsory opinion.
solutions.AC9E3LA04-guided-1: A: Our book basket is useful encompasses lifting, reaching and steadiness. B only announces handles, missing the other functions; C overgeneralises all baskets and praise beyond supplied evidence.
solutions.AC9E3LA04-guided-2: B A F: Our pots have clear labels. Each pot has a plant name beside it. The names help us identify the plants. Then D C E: Our watering tools are easy to find. The watering can is kept by the door. A jug stands beside the can. The groups are labels/identification and tool locations; the can is introduced before the reference the can in E. Other orders may work if focus and references remain clear.
solutions.AC9E3LA04-guided-3: First break shifts from lunchtime plan to after-lunch discovery. The single-sentence middle paragraph emphasises the unexpected empty shelf and can create suspense before the explanation. Length alone is not the rule.
solutions.AC9E3LA04-tricky-1: No. Narratives may mark shifts in time, place, event, speaker or emphasis without an explicit informative topic opening.
solutions.AC9E3LA04-tricky-2: No. Independent focused paragraphs can sometimes change order if references and meaning still work; explain the reader effect rather than asserting one universal order.
solutions.AC9E3LA04-tricky-3: No automatic deletion. Move useful unrelated information to an appropriate paragraph and repair references if needed.
solutions.AC9E3LA05-guided-1: Materials is the specific relevant subheading. The hidden box may prompt an expectation that a concealed box will matter/be found; the actual chapter must establish contents/events, which the title does not prove.

AC9E3LA05-guided-2.expected_content: Follow Where to enter; matching heading Where to enter and Use the gate beside the shed confirm it. Return to garden menu should reach the menu. Specific label predicts entry information whereas More does not.
AC9E3LA05-guided-2.status: CONTENT CRITERIA SAVED; actual link operation HOLD pending working stimulus

AC9E3LA05-guided-3.reason: Actual print/digital tool-storage cards absent. Need exact page route, link words and trowel destination sentence; do not invent trowel location.

solutions.AC9E3LA05-tricky-1: Yes. A broad heading identifies the main area; a subheading narrows the information need within it.
solutions.AC9E3LA05-tricky-2: No. Next depends on the prepared text's sequence/current position and must be checked at the actual destination.
solutions.AC9E3LA05-tricky-3: Only a cautious expectation about a hidden box; no reliable contents or events can be established without the chapter.

faq.AC9E3LA01-faq-1: Ask group members to restate the agreed plan/their own first action, clarify discrepancies and invite a contribution or pass. A yes/no Do you understand? is weaker evidence.
faq.AC9E3LA01-faq-2: A Welcome to Country is delivered by Traditional Owners or Aboriginal/Torres Strait Islander people permitted by Traditional Owners; anyone may offer an Acknowledgement. Follow local checked guidance and distinguish the purposes/roles. Consequential cultural claim requires authoritative source check after blind phase.
faq.AC9E3LA02-faq-1: A helping verb such as could, might or must which can express possibility, requirement and related meanings with the main verb. Interpret the full context.
faq.AC9E3LA02-faq-2: Yes, if both are defensible with the actual text and each explains its evidence; unsupported labels are not automatically valid.
faq.AC9E3LA03-faq-1: Point to how the text is organised and its language, then explain how those choices help its purpose/reader.
faq.AC9E3LA03-faq-2: Yes. A text can combine informing, recounting, explaining or persuading, so analyse the supplied passage rather than relying only on labels.
faq.AC9E3LA04-faq-1: It develops the paragraph's actual focus through relevant explanation, description or an example; mere same-topic mention may be too loose.
faq.AC9E3LA04-faq-2: Read the whole repaired text, check one clear focus per group, sensible order/references and no loss of useful meaning; explain how the repair helps the reader.
faq.AC9E3LA05-faq-1: A selectable connection leading to another destination such as a section/page. Useful link words predict its content; verify what opens.
faq.AC9E3LA05-faq-2: They can use related headings but different routes: page references/contents versus active links/menus. Comparing them teaches choosing a route and checking information rather than guessing.

activity_tier_criteria.AC9E3LA01: Demonstrate planned turn convention, invitation allowing pass, restatement, relevant suggestion/question, specific reasoned feedback, negotiated topic change and shared-action check. Adult-supported single turn versus whole exchange versus chaired-meeting transfer are distinct meaningful tiers. Extra cards HOLD.
activity_tier_criteria.AC9E3LA02: Make context-valid changes for less compulsion, changed evaluation and stronger pleasure, explaining distinct meanings. Own rule: We must close the paint pots. Own prediction: The paint might be dry tomorrow. Adult choice support versus three explained changes versus two contrasting contextual versions; extra revision cards HOLD.
activity_tier_criteria.AC9E3LA03: For each actual card identify purpose, structure and language clue and connect choices to reader function; compare same-object information versus argument. Starter supported contrasting pair, Core full comparisons, Stretch original persuasive conversion with introduction/two relevant reasons/conclusion. Actual cards HOLD.
activity_tier_criteria.AC9E3LA04: Sort exact sentences into focused groups, choose useful opening, resolve reference and justify a narrative break. Starter supported sorting/opening choice, Core arranging with reasons, Stretch alternative defensible ordering/break with effect. Exact cards HOLD.
activity_tier_criteria.AC9E3LA05: Use actual print and working digital routes for three needs; record confirming sentences and sensible replacement Tools storage for vague More. Starter supported two routes, Core actual navigation/reasoning, Stretch improved accurate label preserving destination. Exact cards and interaction HOLD.
